name: Antoni Moore
description: Named contributor in sourced geospatial conference and publication records.
story: GeoCart 2014 accepted abstracts, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Geographical vector agents for supervised image classification”; “Geovisual data mining of dolphin space-time trajectories”; “Hydrologically adaptive regular tessellations for urban drainage modelling”.

GeoCart 2016 conference programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Routes to Dunedin secondary schools and students' perceptions of safety”; “Representations of geography in New Zealand First World War cartoons”; “Visualisation of active transport data”; “An augmented-reality sand-based 3D terrain interface”.

Cartographies of change: GeoCart 2018 proceedings, National Library of New Zealand record 40158196 lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Extracting city objects with vector agents”; “Dissecting the GPS track”; “Local farm knowledge mapping for heritage and biological research”; “GIS analysis of active transport data in Dunedin”; “Spatial assessment of school neighbourhoods and adolescent travel in Dunedin”; “Spatial analysis and geovisualisation for active transport”; “A tangible interface for land development teaching”.
GeoCart session 1 programme, New Zealand Cartographic Society (archived programme page) lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Spatial data quality and veracity”.

New Zealand Geospatial Research Conference 2022 programme, Massey Geoinformatics Collaboratory lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Modelling climate-related coastal flooding hazards and residential property values”; “Geographically weighted logistic regression for active transport”.

Spatial aspects of a comparative study of active transport to school and motorized transport, SIRC NZ 2013 repository record, University of Otago lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Spatial aspects of a comparative study of active transport to school and motorized transport”.
SIRC NZ 2013 GIS and remote sensing proceedings citations, University of Otago lists Antoni Moore as an author of “Geographical vector agent modelling for image classification”.
GIScience 2025 accepted abstracts, official conference programme lists Antoni Moore as an author of “A comparison of two steering laws for unconstrained immersive hybrid navigation”.
